title: Add read-only Product image library over existing image slots
description: Add a user-visible, read-only Product image library over the three image-reference fields already present in Product master data. Reuse persisted references only. Do not upload, replace or delete OSS objects, introduce new storage credentials, perform server-side fetching of arbitrary URLs, add production schema, or deploy.
acceptance_criteria: Users can open a paged Product image library that displays the existing three image slots together with Product code, name and specification.
Users can filter by Product code or name and distinguish products with images, partially populated image slots and products without images.
Missing or broken references render a safe placeholder and do not prevent the remaining Product records from loading.
Only approved local or HTTP/HTTPS reference forms are rendered as images; unsafe schemes and untrusted markup are shown as unavailable text and are never executed.
The application does not fetch arbitrary image URLs on the server, expose storage credentials, or infer ownership or authorization for an OSS object.
The library does not upload, overwrite, delete or otherwise mutate production OSS objects and does not rewrite the existing Product image fields.
The query is bounded or paged and avoids per-product database queries for normal library use.
Unit/integration tests cover full, partial, empty, broken and unsafe image references, filters, paging and non-mutation; safe validation passes.
Browser/UI acceptance is recorded as deferred during development according to project policy.

scenarios: Open the Product image library, filter by Product code, and verify all populated image slots are displayed with their Product context.
Inspect Products with missing, broken and unsafe image references and verify placeholders are shown without script execution or any upload/delete action.

human_gate.reason: Read-only presentation of existing Product image references. Production OSS upload, replacement, deletion, credential use, deployment and release remain outside task scope and behind human gates.
